deals.evidence: Red Bull, the energy drink brand, has agreed to buy the Major League Soccer’s MetroStars in a deal that could reach a reported $50 million.
deals.headline: Red Bull buys the MetroStars from AEG and rebrands the club
deals.summary: Red Bull agreed to buy the MetroStars from AEG in a deal Chief Marketer reported could reach $50m (reported, not confirmed), taking a 50% stake in the planned Harrison stadium alongside AEG. Pre-2015; listed because it is the current owner's entry.

deals.evidence: Red Bull, a beverage maker, bought full control of the stadium—previously known as Red Bull Arena—in 2007.
deals.headline: Red Bull takes full control of the Harrison stadium
deals.summary: Red Bull bought full control of the stadium (then Red Bull Arena). Pre-2015; terms not stated.

deals.evidence: The contract values the rights for the Harrison, N.J., venue in the nine figures (more than $100 million), according to a source familiar with the agreement.
deals.headline: Red Bull Arena renamed Sports Illustrated Stadium in 13-year naming-rights deal
deals.summary: 13-year naming-rights partnership; Sportico, citing a source, says the contract is worth more than $100m in total (nine figures).

operating_result.evidence: The estimates of teams’ revenue and operating income (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization) reflect the 2025 season
operating_result.source_name: Forbes (estimate), The Most Valuable MLS Teams 2026

stadium_owner.detail: Owned by Red Bull, the club's owner: Red Bull took a 50% stake in the Harrison stadium with AEG in 2006 and bought full control in 2007. Known as Red Bull Arena until a 13-year naming-rights deal with Sports Illustrated Tickets from the 2025 season.
stadium_owner.evidence: Red Bull, a beverage maker, bought full control of the stadium—previously known as Red Bull Arena—in 2007.

name: Red Bull New York
